newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine protestors lift road block after pledges.
newsitem.headline: Argentine protestors lift road block after pledges.

text.p: Thousands of northeastern Argentine protesters Wednesday lifted a weekend blockade of a highway to the Bolivian border after the provincial government promised measures to create jobs.

Argentine television showed the demonstrators dragging away bundles of wood they had used to block national route 34 and sweeping up the ashes of burnt rubber tires after protest representatives reached an agreement with officials.

The people of the impoverished towns of Tartagal, General Mosconi and Aguaray near the Bolivian border in the province of Salta began their roadblock last Wednesday, cutting off traffic to Bolivia and to the city of Salta 220 miles (350 km) south.

Salta's Employment Minister Gilberto Oviedo told the state-run Telam news agency that the government had promised measures including funds from the government-owned Banco Nacion to refinance the debts of local business.
"We will start to work on the implementation of these measures tomorrow," Oviedo said.

Argentina's national unemployment rate is 17.3 percent, but poverty is much more acute in provinces like Salta. The area of Tartagal has suffered from job cuts by former state oil firm YPF and over 50 percent of the local workforce is unemployed.

The demonstration has generally been peaceful, but the Argentine Press Association complained that protestors annoyed at media coverage of the events have twice seized large numbers of copies of the local El Tribuno newspaper and burnt them.
